extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in wartime/frontline news and analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and analyzing frontline military operations (air, land, naval) for a general audience: combining official communiqués, correspondent dispatches, tactical details, strategic context, and human-interest items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on official communiques and special bulletins
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute frontline updates to official sources such as 'the special communique' and 'the regular communique' when reporting movements, captures, and operational results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article repeatedly cites 'the special communique' and 'the regular communique' for authoritative statements (e.g., 'The special communique said', 'The regular communique earlier said'). Use such official bulletins as primary sourcing for major operational announcements and to anchor reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Associated Press/field dispatches and correspondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate Associated Press dispatches and on-the-ground correspondent reports to provide immediacy and eyewitness detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text: 'An Associated Press dispatch from the front said...', 'a field dispatch from an Associated Press correspondent with the British First Army said...'. Cite the correspondent/dispatch and use their field observations (troop movements, specific engagements) to complement official communiqués.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide precise operational details (locations, distances, unit names, numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report exact place names, distances, unit designations, counts (sorties, prisoners, ships sunk), and dates to give specificity to battlefield coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece includes specifics such as 'Massicault, fifteen miles from Tunis', 'more than 2,000 sorties', 'the Americans were only four miles...', 'took more than 300 prisoners'. Use such precise figures and geographic markers to situate the reader and quantify progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze strategic significance rather than merely repeating rumors
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextualize reported events for their strategic implications (shipping routes, invasion possibilities, wider campaign effects) instead of focusing solely on verifying every rumor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article states 'The purpose of this article isn't to debate whether the Boche report is true. The point is that it wouldn't be surprising...' and goes on to discuss Mediterranean shipping, Sicily/Sardinia invasion possibilities and broader implications. Emphasize what developments mean for the campaign even when some reports are uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document air control and operational results (air domination, aircraft destroyed, sorties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report measures of air power and outcomes: claims of 'air domination', numbers of enemy aircraft destroyed, sorties flown, and the effects of bombing on targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Allied airmen had "complete air domination,"', 'seventeen enemy aircraft were destroyed', 'Northwest African Air Forces ... sank two ships and severely damaged seven more', 'a record of more than 2,000 sorties'. Include these metrics to show air campaign effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include authoritative quotes from commanders and officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Use direct quotes from senior commanders, political leaders, and local officials to add authority, summary judgment, and perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article uses quotations such as Spaatz's summary, Gen. Henri Giraud's announcements, and other commander comments. These quotes can 'sum up' situations or provide official interpretation and should be attributed clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate combined-arms reporting (air, naval, artillery, infantry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how air, naval, artillery, and ground forces interact — e.g., air strikes, artillery barrage paving way for infantry/armor advances, naval sinkings supporting operations ashore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text interweaves descriptions: 'a big artillery barrage and accompanied by one of the heaviest Allied air actions', 'Flying Fortresses sank an ammunition ship', and ground advances supported by air. Reporters should show coordination and mutual effects among arms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include human-interest and morale details (decorations, personal anecdotes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bolster operational reporting with human stories: lists of medals, personal anecdotes of crews, rescue tales, and individual acts of heroism to convey human cost and morale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece lists decorated personnel (Silver Stars, Purple Hearts), recounts crew experiences (Krell and Knight's forced landing), and describes the awarding of medals. Use such items to personalize the larger military narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame reports chronologically and geographically
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchor accounts in time and place: give dates, fronts, and the progression of actions across specified sectors to help readers follow the campaign's development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article opens with datelines (e.g., 'Allied Headquarters in North Africa, May 6') and repeatedly references fronts (Tunisian front, Medjerda Valley, Bizerte, Tebourba). Maintain clear chronology and geography throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid descriptive language to convey intensity and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ vivid, concrete language—fires, smoke, 'rain of artillery', 'smoking and burning'—to convey the intensity and physical effects of combat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrases in the text like 'rain of Allied artillery and infantry blows', 'flying Fortresses left fires raging in waterfront and railway wreckage', or 'one huge explosion ... a column of smoke two miles high' demonstrate how descriptive language illustrates impact. Use such prose judiciously to communicate urgency and scale.
